content:
sam: Running into weird client-side throttling where 429 + quota headers together cause us to sleep too long. Repro attached.

julie: Can you paste the headers exactly? 429 handling is messy across endpoints.

sam: Example sequence: response A -> 200 with `x-quota-remaining: 1200`, `x-quota-reset: 1710000000`; response B -> 200 with `x-quota-remaining: 1100`; response C -> 429 with `Retry-After: 1699999999` (epoch) and no quota headers. Our current logic treats Retry-After epoch as seconds and sleeps for ~50 years.

pete: Yikes. We have two bugs there: retry-after parsing and mixing header-derived resets with explicit Retry-After.

lina: Our parse currently does `float(value)` and treats > 1e6 as epoch, but the edge conditions aren't covered. Also we should prioritize `x-quota-reset` over Retry-After if both exist.

sam: Proposed tiny patch:
```
def parse_retry_after(v: str) -> float:
    # return seconds to wait
    try:
        n = float(v)
    except ValueError:
        return 0.0
    # heuristics: if value looks like epoch (>= 1e9) -> seconds = value - now
    if n > 1e9:
        return max(0.0, n - time.time())
    return n
```
This avoids the huge sleep.

julie: Also for quota merging we should avoid per-response atomic updates on a shared dict. Two options: (1) swap to an `asyncio.Lock` around the cache, or (2) make header parsing pure and push diffs to an `asyncio.Queue` consumed by a single writer. Option 2 scales better under high concurrency.

pete: I prefer the queue + writer so we keep middlewares non-blocking. Implementation idea:
```
# consumer task
async def _quota_writer(queue, cache):
    while True:
        diff = await queue.get()
        # apply diff atomically in one coroutine
        cache['remaining'] = min(cache.get('remaining', diff['remaining']), diff['remaining'])
        cache['reset'] = max(cache.get('reset', 0), diff['reset'])
```
Middlewares call `queue.put_nowait(parse_quota_headers(resp.headers))`.

lina: Typing: expose a public `class RateCache(Protocol)` and `class AsyncRateCache` impl. Document methods: `async def submit(self, headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> None` and `async def peek(self) -> Mapping[str, int]`. That gives us clear surface contract.

sam: For ergonomics I also propose `client.add_rate_cache(cache)` API so SDK users can opt-in their own storage/metrics. Default should be simple in-memory writer.

julie: Tests: add a stress test that spawns 200 tasks that call `client.chat.completions.create` and randomly returns headers including epoch Retry-After, float Retry-After, and missing quota headers. Assert we never end up with negative remaining and that sleeps are < 60s on average.

pete: PR inbound: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/1002 (WIP) adds parse_retry_after, async queue writer, and RateCache protocol.

ci-bot: PR #1002 0% complete - lint/pytests running.

lina: One more nit: document header names we read and caveat that upstreams may send `X-Quota-Remaining` vs `x-quota-remaining`. Normalize keys to lower-case.

sam: Good catch. Also log a debug line when we parse a Retry-After epoch to help operators.

julie: For backward compat, make the queue writer optional behind `client.options.rate_merge_mode = "none" | "lock" | "queue"`. Default `queue`.

pete: Agree. We'll keep `lock` for minimal change path.

ci-bot: PR #1002 - all tests passed on ubuntu/py3.11.

sam: Will follow up with changelog entry and short example under `examples/async_rate_limit.py`. Thanks everyone.
